Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

exception noun

also make an exception, without exception, no exceptions, an exception to the rule, exempt

classical

Cic. Lael. 17: sine ūllā exceptiōne (Lewis & Short)

exceptiō, exceptiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an exception, a restriction

Lewis & Short: good prose and very frequent, especially in Cicero, most often in sine (ūllā) exceptiōne and cum exceptiōne. In law it is the defendant’s plea against the plaintiff’s claim.

Other words

  • excipiō, excipere, excēpī, exceptum — make an exception of, leave out

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 4.15: hōsce ego hominēs excipiō et sēcernō libenter (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.10.50: exceptō quod, except that (Lewis & Short)

    Its everyday senses are others: to catch (a ball), to receive or welcome (a guest), to follow on. The ablative absolute exceptō or exceptā with a noun means “with the exception of” (see except).

Examples

  • cōnsiliōrum, voluntātum sine ūllā exceptiōne commūnitās

    a sharing of plans and wishes without any exceptionCic. Lael. 17 (Lewis & Short)

  • hōsce ego hominēs excipiō et sēcernō libenter

    these men I gladly make an exception of and set apartCic. Cat. 4.15 (Lewis & Short)

  • exceptō quod nōn simul essēs, cētera laetus

    happy in everything else, except that you were not with meHor. Ep. 1.10.50 (Lewis & Short)

  • Hodiē tē excipiam: post cēnam lūdere licet.

    Today I’ll make an exception for you: you may play after supper.composed

See also except, rule, unless.

SourcesLewis & Short: exceptio · Lewis & Short: excipio

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
